discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of individual electron spins in solid-state defects, establishing diamond colour centres as a platform for quantum sensing and quantum networks
subfield: Solid-state quantum optics and quantum technologies
motivation: The nominees showed that a single electron spin in a solid, the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, can be isolated, read out optically and coherently controlled, even at room temperature. Wrachtrup's optical detection of magnetic resonance of single defects and demonstrations of coherent spin control and entanglement with nuclear spins opened the field. Awschalom established ultrafast and coherent manipulation of single defect spins and extended the concept to technologically mature materials such as silicon carbide. Lukin combined quantum optics with these spins, introducing nanoscale magnetometry, nuclear-spin quantum registers and spin-photon interfaces for quantum networks. Together they turned a crystal imperfection into a controllable quantum system. This platform now underpins nanoscale magnetic imaging in condensed matter and biology, quantum-network nodes, and a broad search for new spin-photon defects in many materials. It is a clear case of fundamental single-quantum-system physics with transformative reach.
